main_text.p: rendi, & salutem omnium tûm consilio domi, tûm armis foris tuendi, si laudem vel ex hostis ore mereatur, quanto plus officii postulat à cive? Etenim ut {a}AssuerusEsth. 6. 1. rex è Chronicorum suorum lectione excitatus est ad rei regè dignæ meditationem, & præmium Mardochæo pro bene-facto tribuendum: sic tuæ in historiis, & sacris, quibus primum locum jure defers, & aliis evoluedis cogitationes ad usum vitæ cuncta revocant; ut inde (quemadmodū recte monet {b}Livius)Lib. 1. tibi tuaque reipublicæ, quod imitere, capias; inde fœdum inceptu, fœdum exitu, quod vites. Itaque {c}Philippi CominæiChron. Ludovic. XI. cap. 34. dictum, plus in unico libro videri tribus mensi-bus, quàm viginti ætates hominum observent, in te experientia docuit verum esse. Quod prudentissimo suo judicio comprobauit Serenissima Princeps, quum in lectissimorum Consiliariorum cœtum te ascivit, nihilo majorem ætatis rationem habens, quàm annalis legis habuerunt Romani in Scipione Æmiliano. page.notes: Marginal notes are in the right margin and were placed beside their lines. The note for c reads "XI. cap. 34." with a separate "34." on the next line; I merged the two into one note as the most likely reading. The epitome book number in note f ("lib.90." or "lib.50.") is hard to read; I have read it as 50 with a question mark. The ornament at the foot before the page number is not transcribed. Words at the line ends are hyphenated as printed (bene-facto, mensi-bus, Po-lybiúsque, Xenophon-tis, sum-). The last line ends mid-word, and the text continues on the next page.
